region: Vellore region, Tamil Nadu, India (district and surrounding dry-tropical landscape)
scope_note: A curated, sourced starter checklist for plants likely to be encountered across the wider Vellore region. It is not an exhaustive flora or a claim that every listed plant occurs at every site. Presence is a library observation state, not a model prediction. A GBIF Plantae occurrence search for the Vellore-area bounding box returned 1,895 records and 300 species facets when checked on 2026-09-05; GBIF coverage and publisher licenses vary, so that result is context for breadth rather than a complete flora census.

species.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent and widely cultivated in tropical settlements.
species.conservation_status: Not threatened in the cited Kew profile
species.ecology: Large tropical strangling fig; aerial roots can develop into additional trunks.
species.short_notes: A very large tree with aerial prop roots and leathery, prominently veined leaves.

knowledge.text: Banyan is a large strangling fig native to the Indian subcontinent; aerial roots hang from branches and can develop into additional trunks.

species.native_status: Native range includes India from southeast Pakistan to Myanmar.
species.ecology: Tropical fig associated with warm forests, open ground and cultivated sacred sites.
species.short_notes: Recognizable by its heart-shaped leaves with a long tapering tip; commonly planted around temples.

knowledge.text: The native range of sacred fig extends from southeast Pakistan to Myanmar and includes India, Nepal and Bangladesh.

species.native_status: Native range is southwestern India; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
species.ecology: Tropical food tree with inflorescences and large fruits produced on main branches and trunk.
species.short_notes: Look for large rough fruits attached directly to the trunk or major limbs and broad glossy leaves.

knowledge.text: Jackfruit has a native range in southwestern India and is now widely cultivated in tropical regions.

species.native_status: Native range includes India and tropical and subtropical Asia; commonly grown in South Asian homes.
species.conservation_status: Least concern in the cited Kew profile
species.ecology: Aromatic herb of warm open habitats and household gardens.
species.short_notes: A strongly aromatic, branching herb; leaves may be green or purple and stems are often hairy.

knowledge.text: Holy basil is an aromatic herb widely cultivated around South Asian homes and temples; the cited Kew profile places its native range in India and tropical Asia.

species.native_status: Native to northern India and Pakistan; now widely cultivated throughout the tropics.
species.conservation_status: Least Concern (IUCN assessment cited by Kew)
species.ecology: Fast-growing drought-tolerant tree cultivated in gardens and farms; compound leaves and long pods are distinctive.
species.short_notes: Compound leaves, pale fragrant flowers and long slender pods give this tree its familiar local name.

knowledge.text: Moringa is native to northern India and Pakistan and is now widely cultivated throughout the tropics.

species.native_status: Native range extends from Bhutan to India; cultivated widely for fragrant flowers.
species.ecology: Fragrant evergreen shrub grown in warm gardens and used as an ornamental and cultural flower.
species.short_notes: Small glossy leaves and intensely fragrant white flowers, often double in cultivated forms.

knowledge.text: Arabian jasmine has a native range from Bhutan to India and is introduced or cultivated in many tropical regions.

species.native_status: Native to Kerala and Tamil Nadu in India.
species.ecology: A region-specific Western Ghats tree; a low-confidence image match must not be treated as a confirmed record.
species.short_notes: Included to keep a conservation-sensitive Tamil Nadu species visible in the regional checklist.

knowledge.text: Syzygium microphyllum has a native range in India, specifically Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

species.native_status: Kew records a native range from Assam to Indo-China and records India as introduced; widely planted across India.
species.conservation_status: Not threatened (Kew prediction cited on POWO)
species.ecology: A drought-tolerant tropical tree common in streets, farms and dry woodland plantings.
species.short_notes: Feathery pinnate leaves, small white flowers and yellow drupes; avoid treating a common name as a taxonomic confirmation.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Azadirachta indica as a tree of the wet tropical biome, native from Assam to Indo-China, with India listed among introduced areas.

species.native_status: Kew records a native range from Assam to southern China and widespread cultivation, including India.
species.conservation_status: Data deficient in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Evergreen tropical fruit tree with leathery lance-shaped leaves, terminal panicles and large drupes.
species.short_notes: Leaves are often coppery when young; fruit size, shape and colour vary greatly among cultivars.

knowledge.text: Mangifera indica is a tree native from Assam to southern China and is widely cultivated in tropical regions, including India.

species.native_status: Origin is uncertain; Kew describes it as widely cultivated throughout the tropics and possibly native to tropical Africa, Madagascar and/or India.
species.conservation_status: Not currently of conservation concern in the cited Kew profile
species.ecology: Large seasonally dry tropical tree with many small leaflets and brown, acidic, sausage-shaped pods.
species.short_notes: The combination of fine paired leaflets and brown curved pods is useful, but fruiting is seasonal.

knowledge.text: Kew describes tamarind as a tree up to about 30 m with paired leaflets and brown pods containing acidic pulp; its origin is uncertain because it has been cultivated since ancient times.

species.native_status: Native to western and southern India and Sri Lanka.
species.ecology: Seasonally dry tropical tree known for long hanging racemes of yellow flowers and cylindrical dark pods.
species.short_notes: Golden flower racemes are conspicuous in season; compound leaves and long woody pods persist after flowering.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Cassia fistula as native to western and southern India and Sri Lanka.

species.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent.
species.ecology: Thorny or unarmed tree with trifoliate leaves and hard-shelled fruits; found in warm tropical and subtropical habitats.
species.short_notes: Three-foliolate leaves, aromatic foliage and hard round fruits help distinguish it from other garden trees.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Aegle marmelos as a tree of the Indian subcontinent with digitately trifoliolate leaves and hard-shelled fruits containing orange-red pulp.

species.native_status: Native from tropical and subtropical Asia to the western Pacific, including India.
species.ecology: Shrub or tree often associated with seasonally dry habitats; distinctive thick-walled flattened pods.
species.short_notes: Glossy compound leaves and flattened, thick-walled pods; also known in India as karanja.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Pongamia pinnata as native from tropical and subtropical Asia to the western Pacific, including India.

species.native_status: Native from southern China to tropical Asia, including India.
species.ecology: Seasonally dry tropical shrub or small tree with thick leaves, milky latex and waxy star-like flowers.
species.short_notes: Milky sap can irritate skin and eyes; observe without handling and never infer edibility from an identification.

knowledge.text: Kew records Calotropis gigantea as native from southern China to tropical Asia, including India, and describes it as a shrub or tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome.

species.native_status: Native to tropical America; introduced into India according to Kew distribution data.
species.ecology: Thorny aromatic shrub that can form dense stands in disturbed ground and dry woodland margins.
species.short_notes: Small clustered flowers change colour as they age; leaves are rough and aromatic. Treat this as an invasive-watch entry, not a recommendation for planting.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Lantana camara as native to tropical America and introduced into India.

species.native_status: Native range is Central Malesia to the southwest Pacific; cultivated widely in India.
species.ecology: Tall unbranched palm with a smooth trunk, crown of pinnate leaves and familiar fibrous fruit.
species.short_notes: A palm, not a tree with branches: the leaf crown and smooth leaning trunk are diagnostic at a distance.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Cocos nucifera as a palm distinguished by a smooth slender trunk, crown of pinnate leaves and its well-known fruit; its native range is Central Malesia to the southwest Pacific.

species.native_status: Native to tropical and subtropical Asia, including India; cultivated bananas derive from this wild ancestor.
species.ecology: Giant herb arising from a rhizome; overlapping leaf bases form a pseudostem and large leaves.
species.short_notes: The apparent trunk is a pseudostem made of leaf bases; wind-split leaves are common and not necessarily disease.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Musa acuminata as the wild ancestor of cultivated banana, a giant herb with a pseudostem formed from overlapping leaf bases; its native range includes India.

species.native_status: A cultigen with a native range listed by Kew as Peru; introduced and cultivated in India.
species.ecology: Small fruit tree with pale peeling bark, opposite aromatic leaves and edible berries.
species.short_notes: Pale coppery bark and strongly veined leaves are useful field clues; fruit colour varies by cultivar.

knowledge.text: Kew describes guava as a small tree up to about 12 m with pale brown or copper-coloured flaking bark and elliptic leaves; its distribution includes introduced India.

species.native_status: Native to northeast tropical Africa; introduced into India according to Kew distribution data.
species.ecology: Fast-growing shrub or small tree of disturbed ground with large palmately lobed leaves and spiny seed capsules.
species.short_notes: Seeds are highly toxic if chewed; use the visual record only and do not handle fruit or recommend medicinal use.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Ricinus communis as native to northeast tropical Africa and introduced into India; it is a shrub or tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome.

species.native_status: Native to the Americas; introduced into India. Prosopis juliflora is a widely used alternative name.
species.ecology: Armed shrub or tree that can naturalize in dry disturbed ground and compete with native vegetation.
species.short_notes: Long spines and small paired leaflets are useful clues; the accepted Kew name is Neltuma juliflora, formerly Prosopis juliflora.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Neltuma juliflora and lists Prosopis juliflora as a synonym; its native range is in the Americas and India is listed among introduced areas.

species.native_status: Native to Central America through Venezuela and Ecuador; introduced into India.
species.conservation_status: Least concern in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Large spreading tropical street and shade tree with bipinnate leaves that can fold in low light.
species.short_notes: Very broad crown and tiny paired leaflets; commonly planted as a large avenue or campus shade tree.

knowledge.text: Kew describes Samanea saman as a tropical tree often used as a street tree; its native range is Central America to Venezuela and Ecuador and India is an introduced area.

species.native_status: Native to Mexico through Venezuela; introduced and cultivated in India.
species.conservation_status: Least concern in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Small seasonally dry tropical tree with thick branches, milky latex and fragrant flowers.
species.short_notes: Flowers are fragrant and variable in colour; milky sap can irritate and should not be handled.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online records Plumeria rubra as native from Mexico to Venezuela and introduced into India.

species.native_status: A cultivated hybrid; Kew lists it as a cultigen and records it in India.
species.ecology: Shrub grown in warm gardens; large showy flowers occur in many cultivated colour forms.
species.short_notes: A garden hybrid rather than a single wild provenance; use flower colour only as supporting evidence, not as a species key.

knowledge.text: Kew treats Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis as a cultivated hybrid (a cultigen) and records it as introduced or cultivated in India.

species.native_status: Native to the Caribbean region; widely cultivated as an ornamental in tropical gardens.
species.ecology: Small tropical tree with thick branches, leathery leaves and milky latex; commonly planted for fragrant flowers.
species.short_notes: The campus photographs support Plumeria obtusa more than a cultivar-level identification; white-flowered frangipani forms can still be difficult to separate without a complete leaf and flower view.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Plumeria obtusa as a tropical tree of the Caribbean region and records it as cultivated beyond its native range.

species.native_status: Native from Mexico to northern Peru and Brazil; introduced and cultivated in tropical regions, including India.
species.ecology: Bulbous geophyte of the wet tropical biome, grown for its distinctive white flowers.
species.short_notes: The corona and strap-like leaves are visible in the campus photographs; species-level confidence is moderate because related spider lilies are cultivated.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Hymenocallis littoralis as a bulbous geophyte native from Mexico to northern Peru and Brazil and records it as introduced into India.

species.native_status: Native to tropical Asia; widely cultivated as an ornamental shrub.
species.ecology: Evergreen shrub with opposite leaves and dense terminal clusters of tubular flowers.
species.short_notes: The red clustered flowers in the campus photographs support Ixora coccinea; cultivar names are intentionally not inferred from colour alone.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Ixora coccinea as a shrub native to tropical Asia and records its use as an ornamental plant.

species.native_status: Native to tropical West Africa; widely cultivated as an ornamental plant.
species.ecology: Rhizomatous perennial herb forming upright leaf rosettes; it tolerates dry indoor and garden conditions.
species.short_notes: The accepted Kew name is Dracaena trifasciata; Sansevieria trifasciata is an important horticultural synonym.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Dracaena trifasciata and treats Sansevieria trifasciata as a synonym; it is a rhizomatous plant widely grown as an ornamental.

species.native_status: Native to tropical Asia and widely cultivated in warm gardens.
species.ecology: Rhizomatous perennial herb of tropical habitats with upright leafy stems and terminal inflorescences.
species.short_notes: The campus images support the Costus/spiral-ginger group; Hellenia speciosa is the current Kew name for the species historically called Costus speciosus, but open flowers would improve certainty.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Hellenia speciosa and records Costus speciosus and Cheilocostus speciosus among names used for this plant.

species.native_status: Native from tropical Asia to the western Pacific; widely cultivated for coloured foliage.
species.ecology: Evergreen shrub with a cane-like stem and terminal rosettes of strap-shaped leaves.
species.short_notes: The red-purple foliage supports Cordyline fruticosa; the particular horticultural cultivar is not inferred.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Cordyline fruticosa as an evergreen shrub native from tropical Asia to the western Pacific and widely cultivated outside that range.

species.native_status: Native to the western Pacific and cultivated in tropical gardens.
species.ecology: Evergreen ornamental shrub with opposite leaves and tubular flowers.
species.short_notes: The photographed yellow-netted form is a horticultural selection often sold as ‘Reticulatum’; the catalog joins only the species, not an unsupported cultivar claim.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Pseuderanthemum maculatum as a species of Acanthaceae; cultivar names are not treated as separate species here.

species.native_status: Native to Taiwan and Hainan; widely cultivated as an ornamental shrub.
species.ecology: Evergreen shrub or small tree with palmately compound leaflets, often grown in variegated forms.
species.short_notes: The campus plants are variegated forms of the dwarf umbrella tree; cultivar names are intentionally not assigned.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Heptapleurum arboricola and lists Schefflera arboricola as a synonym; it is a cultivated ornamental shrub outside its native range.

species.native_status: Native to southern tropical America; widely grown as a foliage ornamental.
species.ecology: Low subshrub with opposite leaves marked by contrasting veins; associated with wet tropical habitats.
species.short_notes: The lime-green leaves with dark reticulate veins support Fittonia albivenis; the nursery cultivar is not inferred.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Fittonia albivenis as a subshrub native to southern tropical America and records it as cultivated beyond that range.

species.native_status: Native to tropical America; introduced and naturalized in many tropical regions.
species.ecology: Tendril-bearing herbaceous climber with lobed leaves and distinctive bracted fruits.
species.short_notes: Tendrils, lobed leaves and the bracted fruit support Passiflora foetida; the absence of an open flower limits certainty.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Passiflora foetida as a tendril-bearing climber native to tropical America and records it as introduced in other tropical regions.

species.native_status: Native from Florida and the Caribbean through Mexico to Venezuela; cultivated as an ornamental outside that range.
species.conservation_status: Least concern in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Shrub or tree of the seasonally dry tropical biome with rough alternate leaves and orange funnel-shaped flowers.
species.short_notes: The audit photographs show the rough alternate leaves and wrinkled orange funnel flowers described by NParks; this replaces the earlier Lantana label for that group.

knowledge.text: NParks describes Cordia sebestena as a medium-sized tree with rough, alternate ovate leaves and orange funnel-shaped, wrinkled flowers in terminal panicles.
Kew accepts Cordia sebestena as a shrub or tree native from Florida and the Caribbean through Mexico to Venezuela.

species.native_status: Native from India through Malesia; widely cultivated as an ornamental climber.
species.ecology: Woody climber with opposite leaves and tubular flowers that change colour as they mature.
species.short_notes: The white-to-pink flower sequence in the campus photographs supports Rangoon creeper; Quisqualis indica is an important synonym.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Combretum indicum and lists Quisqualis indica among its synonyms; it is a cultivated ornamental climber.

species.native_status: Native from the southern United States through tropical America; cultivated and naturalized in many tropical regions.
species.ecology: Shrub or small tree with pinnate leaves and terminal clusters of yellow trumpet-shaped flowers.
species.short_notes: The yellow trumpet flowers and serrated pinnate leaflets support Tecoma stans; orange flower colour is treated as a cultivar-level variation, not a separate species.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Tecoma stans as a shrub or tree native to the Americas and records it as introduced or cultivated beyond that range.

species.native_status: Native to eastern Madagascar; widely cultivated as an ornamental palm.
species.ecology: Clustering palm with ringed stems and pinnate fronds, grown widely in tropical landscapes.
species.short_notes: Kew currently accepts Chrysalidocarpus lutescens; Dypsis lutescens remains the common horticultural synonym. Six campus frames appear to show one clump.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Chrysalidocarpus lutescens and lists Dypsis lutescens as a synonym; the species is native to eastern Madagascar and widely cultivated.

species.native_status: Native to tropical Asia, including India, and cultivated in tropical settlements.
species.ecology: Evergreen tree with glossy leaves and fragrant flowers; commonly planted in South Asian towns and campuses.
species.short_notes: The campus sign explicitly names Mimusops elengi; the photographed glossy leaves are consistent with the identification.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Mimusops elengi as a tropical Asian tree and records India within its native range.

species.native_status: Native to tropical America; introduced and invasive in many tropical regions, including India.
species.ecology: Fast-spreading perennial groundcover with yellow flower heads and lobed leaves.
species.short_notes: The yellow daisies and spreading lobed foliage support Sphagneticola trilobata; Wedelia trilobata is a common synonym.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Sphagneticola trilobata and lists Wedelia trilobata as a synonym; it is native to tropical America and introduced elsewhere.

species.native_status: Native to India and Sri Lanka; widely planted as a narrow ornamental tree.
species.ecology: Evergreen tree with a narrow, columnar habit and long drooping leaves.
species.short_notes: The current Kew name is Monoon longifolium; Polyalthia longifolia remains a widely used synonym in horticulture.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Monoon longifolium and records Polyalthia longifolia as a synonym; it is a cultivated ornamental tree in tropical regions.

species.native_status: Native to northeastern Mexico; widely cultivated as a foliage groundcover.
species.ecology: Trailing succulent-stemmed herb with purple leaves, grown as an ornamental groundcover.
species.short_notes: The purple trailing foliage supports Tradescantia pallida ‘Purpurea’; the cultivar is recorded as a horticultural form rather than a separate species join.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Tradescantia pallida and records it as a trailing herb native to northeastern Mexico; purple horticultural forms are widely cultivated.

species.native_status: Native to tropical South America; variegated forms are cultivated as ornamental shrubs.
species.ecology: Evergreen shrub with large opposite leaves and tubular flowers; horticultural forms are grown for marked foliage.
species.short_notes: The close-ups with broad leaves and yellow/cream venation are Sanchezia oblonga, separate from the Pseuderanthemum group. Sanchezia speciosa is a reported horticultural synonym.

knowledge.text: NParks lists Sanchezia oblonga (variegated) as an ornamental shrub and gives Sanchezia speciosa as a synonym.
Kew accepts Sanchezia oblonga as a species of Acanthaceae.

species.native_status: Native from southern Japan and Taiwan through southern China to northern Peninsular Malaysia; cultivated in tropical gardens.
species.conservation_status: Data deficient in the IUCN record shown by Kew
species.ecology: Rhizomatous perennial herb with broad lanceolate leaves; variegated forms are common ornamentals.
species.short_notes: The striped foliage supports Alpinia zerumbet ‘Variegata’; the cultivar is not represented as a separate species. The campus label is joined to this species only as a qualified horticultural form.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Alpinia zerumbet as a rhizomatous geophyte native from southern Japan and Taiwan through southern China to northern Peninsular Malaysia.

species.native_status: Native to southern China and Taiwan; Kew records it as introduced into India.
species.ecology: Small evergreen subshrub or shrub grown as a clipped ornamental, with very small leaves and white flowers.
species.short_notes: The campus run is consistent with Serissa japonica, but Wrightia, gardenia, and other small-leaved white-flowering hedges remain alternatives without a label or closer diagnostic view.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Serissa japonica, native to southern China and Taiwan, and records it as introduced into India.

species.native_status: Native from Mexico to northern South America, southern Florida and the Caribbean; widely cultivated and naturalized beyond its native range.
species.ecology: Shrub or small tree with opposite or whorled leaves and racemes of small flowers, often grown in clipped or yellow-leaved forms.
species.short_notes: The campus label is supported at species level by the Duranta-like hedge and racemes; a named cultivar such as ‘Gold Mound’ is not asserted from foliage colour alone.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Duranta erecta as a shrub or tree native from Mexico to northern South America, southern Florida and the Caribbean, and notes cultivation and naturalization beyond that range.

species.native_status: Native from Tanzania to southern Africa; cultivated beyond its native range, including tropical and subtropical gardens.
species.ecology: Shrub or scrambling climber with pinnate leaves and terminal clusters of orange to scarlet tubular flowers.
species.short_notes: The orange-flowered campus run is kept separate from the yellow-flowered Tecoma stans run. Tecoma capensis is a synonym; no cultivar is inferred.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Tecomaria capensis, native from Tanzania to southern Africa, and lists Tecoma capensis among its synonyms.

species.native_status: Based on Caladium bicolor, native from Central America to Argentina; cultivated forms are grown widely as ornamentals.
species.ecology: Tuberous geophyte with peltate, heart-shaped leaves; cultivated forms have varied blotches, veins and colour patterns.
species.short_notes: The campus photographs support the Caladium bicolor complex at horticultural-group level. This record deliberately does not claim a named cultivar, hybrid parentage, or an unqualified species identification.

knowledge.text: Kew accepts Caladium bicolor and notes that many cultivated forms have varied leaf variegation; the campus label therefore remains a qualified horticultural group rather than a named cultivar.

species.native_status: Native from Peninsular Thailand to Peninsular Malaysia; grown as a tropical ornamental beyond its native range.
species.ecology: Rhizomatous perennial herb with leafy stems and distinctive cone-like, honeycomb inflorescences that develop among the foliage.
species.short_notes: The cone-shaped beehive inflorescences support Zingiber spectabile; Zingiber zerumbet remains a close alternative when the inflorescence is not fully visible.

knowledge.text: Plants of the World Online accepts Zingiber spectabile as a rhizomatous geophyte native from Peninsular Thailand to Peninsular Malaysia.
